newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Mar 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Mar 3.

text.p: - There are 120 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The English-language HONGKONG STANDARD said Chinese President Jiang Zemin had yet to win his spurs even though mililary leaders have pledged to support him. The paper said Jiang was facing huge problems, including ensuring social order and resolving the complex problem of loss-making state enterprises. But if he ruled wisely, Jiang might usher in the most golden era yet in Chinese history, it said.

-- The Chinese-language ECONOMIC JOURNAL said the government work report of the Chinese Premier Li Peng showed some worrying points, and reforming state enterprises was the biggest headache. The paper said the report was wrong in saying that the success of the "one country two systems" principle relied on the efforts of Hong Kong people, because it was up to China to keep its promise on keeping the "two systems" part of the concept.

-- The Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO said that Chinese people were determined to reunify the country and realise the "one country two systems" principle. It said that by supporting chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa, China's leadership with President Jiang Zemin at its core had demonstrated its sincerity of letting Hong Kong people run Hong Kong.
